chat.user: what do you mean by that?

chosen.reply: I mean I will not warm them up with the old mechanics first. The new physics has to be given whole, or it arrives as a rumor someone repeated. So the first thing I say to them is the thing most likely to send them out the door.

others.action: explain the opening move of the course
others.reply: I mean I intend to put the hard thing first, before they have a comfortable picture to hang it on. If I begin gently they will build a small tidy world in their heads, and every lecture after that becomes an argument with furniture they already own. It is easier for me to be careful than to be slow.

That notebook held the middle of Thursday's lecture, and without it I am working from memory in front of a room that expects better. What I meant to open with is the part of the new physics that costs the most to accept, and I will not hand them a softened version of it just because I am tired.
